hook_text: The first farmers never ate pap made from maize. So what did they eat?
clip_script: Giyani, Limpopo, the school garden. Tall sorghum with heavy red-brown heads. Millet, beans and melons. Two learners chase the birds away. This is what early African farmers grew, with iron hoes, when the summer rains came. Maize came much later, from the Americas. They ground the grain on stones for porridge and beer. And at the gate, two Nguni cattle: milk, hides, horns and dung. Cattle were a family's pride.
visual_style: Whiteboard sorghum stalks growing, a hoe digging, a grindstone turning grain into flour, then two cattle walking in.
mood: Bright and earthy, like a sunny morning in a garden.
pacing: Steady, following the farming year from planting to harvest to the kraal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find out if anyone in your family still eats sorghum porridge.
